bias: This is a same-day re-pull roughly 30 minutes after the last run; FRED plumbing data (WALCL, TGA, reserves, RRP, SOFR) is completely unchanged since the H.4.1 vintage doesn't update intraday. The more interesting intraday moves are in credit and vol: ALLY and COF both flipped from negative to solidly positive on the day, and VIX extended its pullback from -1.84% to -3.93%, both consistent with the 'risk assets comfortable with the reflation read' framing from the last run. The one notable fade is DRAM, whose early +5.79% rally collapsed to +0.43% intraday — worth flagging as a reversal rather than a trend continuation. Overall this remains a real-rate-easing, mild-reflation backdrop that risk assets are tolerating well, with credit and equity vol both improving further since the last check.

counterargs.read: Thirty minutes on, the reflation-in-the-rates-market story from the last run is intact and if anything credit and equity vol have both improved further, which doesn't fit a classic inflation-scare risk-off tape. The one thing worth watching is DRAM's sharp intraday fade — from +5.79% to +0.43% — since it's the first crack in an otherwise firm semis/Korea complex today. Not yet broad enough to change the read, but worth confirming on the next run whether it's isolated or spreads to SOXX and the rest of the chain.
